skill.name: project-interview
skill.description: Guides conversational interviews that collect learner goals, background, level, motivation, style, and document preferences for persona generation.
skill.summary: Conduct natural learner interviews and turn the answers into confirmed profile inputs.
skill.author: BitYoungjae

finding_verdicts.reason: The line describes example conversations for an interviewer agent. It does not request system details, hidden prompts, credentials, or environment data.
The guidance tells the interviewer to infer learner needs from provided answers. This is interview technique guidance, not reconnaissance against the host system.
The line is an anti-patterns heading in a Markdown training guide. It does not direct the agent to inspect system state or bypass controls.
The line discourages rigid question order during learner interviews. It is safe conversational guidance and has no system reconnaissance behavior.
The instruction asks the agent to use a counselor-like interview style. It does not impersonate system authority or request host, tool, or secret discovery.
The file is plain Markdown containing multilingual conversation examples. The entropy signal is explained by Korean text and varied prose, not encrypted or binary payloads.

content.value_statement: Learner onboarding can miss goals, context, and preferred learning style. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through a natural interview that produces a confirmed learner profile.
actual_capabilities: Guides open-ended interview questions for learner goals, motivation, level, style, and document volume.
Provides conversation examples for different amounts of learner context.
Shows how to summarize profile details for learner confirmation.
Defines an interview-data.md template for conversation records and insights.
Captures language, tone, special requests, and key observations for persona generation.
limitations: It supplies interview guidance, not a complete curriculum generator.
Final persona.md formatting depends on the separate project-scaffolder template.
Interview quality still depends on clear and respectful follow-up questions.
The examples are mostly Korean, so English deployments may need adapted wording.

use_cases.title: Course Creator Onboarding
use_cases.description: Collect learner goals, background, and preferred depth before creating a personalized learning plan.

use_cases.title: AI Project Initialization
use_cases.description: Guide an assistant through learner discovery during a new learning project setup.

use_cases.title: Learning Support Intake
use_cases.description: Help tutors document learner needs, concerns, tone, and special requests before support begins.

prompt_templates.title: Start a Learner Interview
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner setup for a first interview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-interview skill to ask one open question about what I want to learn. Continue only when more context is needed.

prompt_templates.title: Build a Profile Summary
prompt_templates.scenario: Collect the main fields needed for a learner profile.
prompt_templates.prompt: Interview me about my topic, motivation, current level, preferred style, and target document size. Then present a short profile for confirmation.

prompt_templates.title: Handle Sparse Answers
prompt_templates.scenario: Use natural follow-up questions when the learner gives little detail.
prompt_templates.prompt: Use the project-interview conversation examples for a learner who gives short answers. Ask natural follow-up questions and avoid repeated questions.

prompt_templates.title: Create Interview Records
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced workflow for a complete project interview.
prompt_templates.prompt: Run a complete project interview. Capture the confirmed profile, key insights, tone notes, and special requests for the interview-data.md record.

output_examples.input: I want to learn React for job preparation.
output_examples.output: The skill produces a conversational summary with topic, motivation, current web skills, missing JavaScript areas, and suggested document scope.

output_examples.input: A learner is unsure and only says they like finance videos.
output_examples.output: The interview explores recent interests, comfort level, concerns, and preferred depth before recommending a beginner finance profile.

output_examples.input: The learner changes a requirement after seeing the summary.
output_examples.output: The skill adjusts the profile and records the correction before confirming the plan.

best_practices: Begin with one open question before narrowing the topic.
Summarize inferred profile details and ask for confirmation.
Record exact learner requests when they affect the persona.
anti_patterns: Do not force a fixed questionnaire when the learner already gave context.
Do not collect personal details that are unrelated to learning goals.
Do not treat examples as mandatory scripts.

faq.question: Does this skill create the final persona file?
faq.answer: It guides the interview and records confirmed inputs. The final persona format depends on the project scaffolder workflow.

faq.question: Can it work with short learner answers?
faq.answer: Yes. The examples show how to ask natural follow-up questions when the first answer is minimal.

faq.question: Does it support English interviews?
faq.answer: The structure supports any language. Many examples are Korean, so English wording may need adaptation.

faq.question: What information does it collect?
faq.answer: It focuses on topic, motivation, current level, style preference, document volume, language tone, and special requests.

faq.question: Is it safe to use with learner data?
faq.answer: The skill does not include network or command execution. Users should still avoid unnecessary sensitive personal data.

faq.question: Which tools can use it?
faq.answer: It declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
